items.title: George "Happy" Schilling Interview, 1957-09-08
items.q: He had this town tied up one time, Jack Lane. Man, everything was the Reliance band

ctx.x: Fake musician. No, there wasn't any legitimate sound like the Robichoke band. No, no, no. Nothing like that.

He had this town tied up one time, Jack Lane. Man, everything was the Reliance band and from there on that was it. I remember when I was a young fellow, before I started to play music, he used to play, you fool around with the guitars and stuff like that. We used to go around with Christian, you know what I'm saying? Christian the fiddle player, his daddy. He was a good trumpet man too, this fiddle player. His daddy had two street bands, each one of his sons run the band. Well, he had everything tied up. It was…

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine, Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine and Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1959-02-27
items.q: Johnny, believe me or not, one time ago I played for a bunch that Shillin was in it.

ctx.x: . The time they play in all that jazz stuff, there's too much breaks in it. Let me see. You know what I mean, Johnny? Yeah. It's not the right time at all at all. Yeah. I'm going to move your chair up. Yeah, that's... That sounded like... Beautiful, beautiful. That sounded like the old-time bands, didn't it? Don't miss it. Don't miss it. It was a lot of fun to play in those days. How come the drum beat came back to you so quickly? It's just... It was just natural that the drum beat came back to you, huh? No,…
What do you want to get out? What do you want to get?

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1957-03-26
items.q: That boy played with me too, George Schilling.

ctx.x: Most versatile musicians playing peppery melodies that are just dance compelling. If it's a hit, we have it.
That boy played with me too, George Schilling.
Happy Schilling. That's a marching band.
